text:
marco: quick sync — thinking through resume semantics for offline + airgapped installs. two modes: streaming checkpoints (resume tokens) and atomic image swap. which should be default?

olivia: default should bias to streaming for bandwidth-limited sites, but we must make the activation step foolproof. include an activation_token that is signed and verifiable offline.

devon: important: resume_token must be monotonic and contain a compact proof of applied-chunks. otherwise we risk applying same chunk twice. suggest token = base64(blake3(root), seq, applied_bitmap).

tanya: operator UX: token expiry is sticky. if token expires, operator must stop and present a manual-restart plan with diff + required approval. no silent retries.

liam: storage note: avoid large journals. prefer per-component small statefiles or CRD fields (k8s) with applyState enum. that keeps disk IO minimal and uses etcd for durability.

kevin: on checksum: blake3 for chunk ids, but include a short salted prefix per-bundle so identical blocks across bundles still dedupe safely when desired.

sara: offline (USB/media) flow idea: produce an "offline-bundle" tarball with manifest.json, chunk-index.bin, and payload shards. manifest includes activation_seq and signer_chain. operator validates signatures locally before applying.

marco: about activation window: two-phase commit seems attractive but messy on restarts. propose: operator obtains a short lease (leader election), writes a fenced marker in CRD, signer-sidecar signs activation, operator atomically flips activated flag. if lease lost -> operator aborts activation and surfaces ERROR.

devon: edge-case: power loss after sign but before writing activated flag. operator must reconcile by checking signed fence blob and fence_state on restart. if fence blob present and lease expired -> require manual thaw.

olivia: GC policy: keep last N activation_seq per component (N=2 default), tombstone older ones after grace window. keep refcounts for content-addressed blocks to make GC safe.

liam: implement refcounts in a tiny sqlite or bolt DB at /var/lib/redwood/refcounts.db. GC pass is incremental and rate-limited. provide a debug endpoint to list top refcounted blocks.

kevin: also add a preflight dry-run that prints estimated fetch size and list of new blocks. very useful for operators to know disk requirements before starting.

sara: testing: need chaos tests for mid-apply powercut, corrupted shard, signer latency, and token expiry. can emulate with a small harness that flips network and kills process mid-apply.

ops-bot: noted: create runbook draft for resume_token expiry and partial-apply recovery. link to incident that motivated this: /incidents/342.

marco: next steps: 1) update RFC to include resume_token format + activation_fence proto, 2) add CRD applyState and lease fields, 3) prototype signer-sidecar offline sign/verify, 4) add dry-run endpoint and GC refcount implementation, 5) author chaos tests. I'll open a branch and tag owners.

olivia: small schema note: manifest should include stable component_id GUIDs to avoid refcount churn on renames.

marco: thanks everyone — want short writeup by EOD so we can fold into RFC. I'll post branch link when ready.
